status_note: active; v0.9.3; Python >=3.10; single-maintainer-led project with a large contributor base; ships a FastAPI Docker server (deploy/docker) with browser pool, Redis job queue, JWT auth, MCP bridge and Prometheus metrics
core_problem: Fetch web pages with a real browser (or plain HTTP), strip them to LLM-ready markdown or schema-extracted JSON, and crawl outward with pluggable strategies, filters and scorers, all behind a single async API and a Docker REST service.
architecture: crawl4ai/async_webcrawler.py AsyncWebCrawler.arun(url, config) orchestrates: optional robots check (RobotsParser, only when CrawlerRunConfig.check_robots_txt=True; default False), cache lookup (async_database.py SQLite; cache_context.CacheMode ENABLED/DISABLED/READ_ONLY/WRITE_ONLY/BYPASS, default BYPASS; cache_validator.py revalidates via ETag/If-None-Match and a head_fingerprint), fetch via async_crawler_strategy.py (AsyncPlaywrightCrawlerStrategy over playwright/patchright with browser_manager.py pools, enable_stealth via playwright-stealth, use_undetected mode, proxy_strategy rotation, user_agent_generator, virtual scroll, js_code hooks, capture_network_requests/capture_console_messages, screenshot/pdf/mhtml) or AsyncHTTPCrawlerStrategy, then content_scraping_strategy.py (LXMLWebScrapingStrategy: cleaned_html, links{internal,external}, media, metadata, tables), markdown_generation_strategy.py (DefaultMarkdownGenerator over html2text with content_source raw_html|cleaned_html|fit_html; convert_links_to_citations produces markdown_with_citations + references_markdown; an optional content_filter produces fit_html/fit_markdown), content_filter_strategy.py (PruningContentFilter: per-block score from text density, link density, tag weights with fixed or dynamic threshold default 0.48; BM25ContentFilter: rank-bm25 against user_query or page metadata; LLMContentFilter), and extraction_strategy.py (JsonCssExtractionStrategy / JsonXPathExtractionStrategy / JsonLxmlExtractionStrategy over a schema {baseSelector, fields:[{name, selector, type: text|attribute|html|nested|list|nested_list|computed|regex}]} with schema validation feedback when baseSelector matches 0 elements and a generate_schema() LLM helper; LLMExtractionStrategy chunks markdown/html by token threshold and calls litellm with a pydantic schema or block instruction, accumulating usages; RegexExtractionStrategy; CosineStrategy). Results are models.CrawlResult (url, html, cleaned_html, fit_html, markdown.{raw,fit,with_citations,references}, links, media, tables, metadata, extracted_content, screenshot, pdf, response_headers, status_code, redirected_url, ssl_certificate, network_requests, console_messages, head_fingerprint, cached_at, cache_status hit|hit_validated|hit_fallback|miss). deep_crawling/: BFSDeepCrawlStrategy, DFSDeepCrawlStrategy, BestFirstCrawlingStrategy with FilterChain (URLPatternFilter, DomainFilter, ContentTypeFilter, ContentRelevanceFilter, SEOFilter) and scorers (KeywordRelevanceScorer, PathDepthScorer, ContentTypeScorer, FreshnessScorer, DomainAuthorityScorer, CompositeScorer); async_dispatcher.py runs arun_many with memory-adaptive concurrency; async_url_seeder.py discovers URLs from sitemaps (robots -> sitemap chain) and Common Crawl index with lastmod-aware caching; adaptive_crawler.py stops when information-foraging coverage saturates; domain_mapper.py builds site maps; link_preview.py scores links. async_configs.py holds BrowserConfig, CrawlerRunConfig (~120 params), LLMConfig, SeedingConfig; a Provenance TRUSTED/UNTRUSTED enum plus UNTRUSTED_ALLOWED_TYPES restricts what a network request body may deserialize on the Docker server (no LLM strategies, proxies, deep-crawl or seeding from untrusted callers). deploy/docker/server.py exposes /crawl, /crawl/stream, /md, /html, /screenshot, /pdf, /execute_js, /llm/{url}, /ask, /schema, /artifacts, /monitor, with crawler_pool.py (permanent/hot/cold browsers), work_queue.py + Redis, webhook.py, mcp_bridge.py, and llm_broker.py.
core_innovation: A crawl result object that carries the page in several parallel, provenance-preserving forms (raw html, cleaned html, fit markdown with citation references, schema-extracted JSON, network/console/ssl evidence) so downstream code can choose the strictest form it needs.
strengths: Deterministic, LLM-free extraction path exists end to end: JsonCssExtractionStrategy with a JSON schema, PruningContentFilter/BM25ContentFilter for fit markdown, and markdown_with_citations that keeps a numbered references list of source URLs, which is exactly what a FactRegistry with `external` provenance needs.

CrawlResult keeps evidence: status_code, response_headers, redirected_url, ssl_certificate, cached_at, cache_status, head_fingerprint; a fact can be stamped with url + fetched_at + http status without extra plumbing.

Deep crawl is a composable pipeline (strategy x FilterChain x scorer) with hard budgets (max_depth, max_pages, DomainFilter) so a competitor-site sample for a niche playbook can be bounded and reproducible.
URL seeding from sitemaps/Common Crawl with lastmod caching gives cheap, polite discovery before any browser is opened; HTTP crawler strategy avoids a browser entirely for static pages.

Docker server is a real service: browser pool, Redis job queue, JWT, Prometheus, and a Provenance/UNTRUSTED allowlist that blocks LLM/proxy/deep-crawl configs from network callers, a good security posture for a sidecar.
Apache-2.0, 84k stars, weekly pushes, extensive docs and CHANGELOG.
weaknesses: Python 3.10+ runtime with 34 deps (playwright, patchright, playwright-stealth, nltk, numpy, lxml, unclecode-litellm fork, shapely/alphashape) and its own browser install; in an Astro/TS pipeline it must run as the Docker sidecar over REST, adding an ops surface.

Anti-bot posture is aggressive by default design (patchright, undetected mode, enable_stealth, user-agent spoofing, magic mode, remove_consent_popups) and robots.txt is opt-in (check_robots_txt=False); using these against competitor sites or Google SERPs is a ToS and reputational risk for an agency product. Google search results scraping violates Google's ToS; GBP data should come from the Places API, not scraping.

LLMExtractionStrategy and generate_schema() are convenience paths that can hallucinate fields; nothing in the library marks which extracted values are literal DOM text versus model output, so provenance must be enforced by us (use only JsonCss/XPath/Regex strategies for facts).

PruningContentFilter and BM25 are heuristic; 'fit markdown' can silently drop the paragraph that held the fact (thresholds 0.48 fixed / dynamic), so facts must be extracted from cleaned_html or raw_html with selectors, not from fit_markdown.
Very large, fast-moving surface (CrawlerRunConfig ~120 params, 2.5k-line config module, adaptive crawler, domain mapper, hub) with breaking minor releases; pin versions and wrap a small facade.
Cache is a local SQLite keyed on URL; no built-in notion of 'fact-level' freshness beyond ETag/head fingerprint, so fetched_at semantics and re-verification cadence are ours to define.
The README's attribution request (badge/text) is not part of the Apache-2.0 grant but is a community expectation; harmless but note it.
patterns_to_steal: CrawlResult multi-form record with evidence fields → fact_registry: define FactSource {url, final_url (redirected_url), status_code, fetched_at (cached_at), etag/head_fingerprint, content_hash, extraction: 'css'|'xpath'|'regex'} and require every `external` Fact to reference one; no FactSource, no Fact.

markdown_with_citations + references_markdown → fact_registry + research: keep the numbered citation map so every quoted claim in a niche playbook draft links back to the exact source URL; quotable=false unless the DOM text is captured verbatim.

JsonCssExtractionStrategy schema {baseSelector, fields[]} with validation feedback → research: author per-source-type extraction schemas (registry pages, association directories, competitor service pages) as versioned YAML in the playbook repo; a schema that matches 0 base elements fails loudly and never returns fabricated fields.

Deep crawl = strategy x FilterChain x scorers with max_depth/max_pages/DomainFilter → research: the competitor-sample job for a niche playbook is a BestFirst crawl bounded to N pages per domain with KeywordRelevanceScorer on service terms, recorded with its config hash so the sample is reproducible for drift review.
Sitemap/Common Crawl seeding with lastmod caching → research drift review: re-check competitor sitemaps by lastmod before re-crawling; drift review only refetches pages whose lastmod or ETag changed.

Provenance TRUSTED/UNTRUSTED config allowlist → agent_orchestration: any config the model or a network caller can produce is deserialized through an allowlist that cannot enable LLM strategies, proxies or unbounded crawls; the same idea applies to model-emitted SiteDefinition patches.
CacheMode + ETag revalidation → fact_registry freshness: store etag/head_fingerprint with each FactSource and revalidate with If-None-Match on a schedule; a 304 renews fetched_at without re-parsing.
patterns_to_avoid: Stealth/undetected/patchright/user-agent spoofing and remove_consent_popups against third-party sites → ToS and ethics exposure for a commercial agency; run with check_robots_txt=True, honest UA, rate limits (mean_delay/max_range), and never bypass bot detection.

Scraping Google SERPs or Google Business Profile pages for 'SERP sampling' or GBP facts → violates Google ToS; use official APIs (Custom Search JSON API, Places API) or licensed SERP providers and record the API as the FactSource.

LLMExtractionStrategy / LLMContentFilter / generate_schema for facts → model-produced values are not provenance-safe; allowed only for exploratory summaries flagged non-quotable and never written to the FactRegistry as `external` facts.
Using fit_markdown as the fact source → pruning can drop the sentence containing the number; extract from cleaned_html via selectors and store the verbatim snippet.

Crawling competitor sites to clone layouts/tokens → explicitly rejected website-cloner pipeline; Crawl4AI is for text facts, positioning language and service inventories only, never screenshots-to-design.
Adopting the whole Docker service surface (/llm, /ask, MCP bridge, hooks) → keep a narrow facade: /crawl with JsonCss schemas and /md with citations; disable LLM endpoints in config.yml.
reusable_patterns: EvidenceBearingFetchRecord: every fetch yields one record carrying the content in multiple fidelities plus transport evidence (status, headers, redirect, tls, timestamps, hashes).
CitationPreservingMarkdown: convert links to numbered citations and keep a references block so derived text retains source URLs.
SchemaSelectorExtraction: declarative {baseSelector, fields[{selector,type}]} extraction that fails loudly on zero matches instead of inventing values.
BoundedBestFirstCrawl: frontier ordered by composable scorers, pruned by a filter chain, capped by depth/pages/domain.
UntrustedConfigAllowlist: deserialize externally supplied configuration only through a strict type/field allowlist with clamped values.
LastmodGatedRecrawl: recrawl only URLs whose sitemap lastmod or ETag changed.
adoption_strategy: Adopt as a research-stage sidecar only, behind a thin TS facade. Run the official Docker image with LLM endpoints disabled, call POST /crawl with CrawlerRunConfig {cache_mode: ENABLED, check_robots_txt: true, mean_delay/max_range for politeness, no stealth, JsonCssExtractionStrategy schemas versioned in the playbook repo, DefaultMarkdownGenerator with citations} and map each CrawlResult into a FactSource record (url, redirected_url, status_code, fetched_at, etag/head_fingerprint, verbatim snippet) before any Fact is created with provenance kind `external`. Use BestFirst deep crawl with DomainFilter and page caps for competitor sampling and sitemap lastmod seeding for drift review. Do not use it for SERP or GBP scraping (use APIs) and never for design/token extraction. Python runtime is acceptable only because it is isolated in a container with a REST contract.
